The synthetic holdout does NOT predict real-photo accuracy on this task — measured, not suspected. run_f's e3-partial (val 0.8466) and its finished e17 model (val 0.8942) score IDENTICALLY on real photos: chesscog_transfer 0.855 -> 0.856, user_photos 0.900 -> 0.894, OVERALL 0.707 -> 0.706. So +4.8pp of holdout gain transferred as 0.0pp where it matters, and 14 of the 20 epochs bought nothing deployable. Consequence: never judge a candidate by val accuracy alone, and do not spend runs on longer training or finer crop-geometry tuning hoping the holdout gain carries — it does not. Corollary for triage: an undertrained checkpoint is a VALID early read on real-photo performance, so score the partial before committing GPU time to convergence.

Pose-aware crop geometry (PoseGeometry h1.9/r0.5, run_f) is ANSWERED and NOT deployed: it trades occupancy for piece type. Versus deployed bbox hr1.6/sp0.15 (run_e) on the same 60 boards, each scored through its own sidecar: chesscog_transfer (unseen real photos) 0.819 -> 0.856 with wrongtype 173 -> 121 (the cross-style decapitation weakness it targeted, -30%), but user_photos 0.938 -> 0.894 with hallucinations 1 -> 12 and occupancy 0.997 -> 0.963 — a taller projected prism swallows part of the neighbouring piece, so empties next to tall pieces get called pieces. Synthetic holdout tied (0.8942 vs 0.898). Pre-registered rule was 'wins both or it does not ship', so run_e stays deployed. The geometry knob is now exhausted in both directions (bbox headroom swept 2026-07-18, pose 2026-08-10); the two models' errors are COMPLEMENTARY, which makes an ensemble the only remaining geometry idea worth GPU time.

export.py prints a full RuntimeError traceback that is NOT a failure: onnxscript's version converter tries opset 18 -> 17, its C-API fallback asserts ('axes_input_to_attribute.h:68 ... No initializer or constant input to node found'), and it then keeps the model at opset 18 and continues. The real success signals come AFTER the traceback — 'exported -> <path>/model.onnx', the written .onnx.meta.json, and 'round-trip OK' with max|torch-onnx| ~3e-07 and argmax agreement. Do not kill a run or re-export on seeing this; check for the round-trip line instead. (A log monitor grepping for 'Traceback|rror' will fire on it — expected noise on every export.)

Per-board display rotation on the live page (BoardCard.svelte): chessground's own 'orientation' prop is a white/black flip through the board centre — it computes file/rank layout for exactly two sides and can never produce a 90-degree-turned picture (this is why Board.svelte already dropped the orientation prop as unused). A 90-degree-step rotation is instead a CSS 'transform: rotate(Ndeg)' on the .board-wrap div that HOSTS the Board component, never touching chessground or the placement — safe because .board-wrap is a square box (--board-size for both dimensions), so rotating it never changes its bounding box or fights the layout. At 90/270 the coordinate labels and piece sprites turn sideways along with everything else inside the wrapper; that's intended (matches physically turning a printed diagram), not a bug to fix. Persistence follows the existing per-key localStorage idiom from camera/state.ts (a key-building function like 'rotationKey(boardId) => board-reader.live.rotation.${boardId}', read/write wrapped in try/catch for private-browsing mode) rather than introducing a shared storage util — this codebase intentionally duplicates that tiny helper per page/component rather than abstracting it. Reading a per-instance prop like board.id inside a $state() initializer must be wrapped in svelte's untrack(), or svelte-check emits state_referenced_locally even when the one-time read is correct (the each-block key already guarantees board.id is stable for that component's lifetime).

The run_e (bbox hr1.6/sp0.15) + run_f (pose h1.9/r0.5) ENSEMBLE works and is deploy-worthy — first geometry-family change to clear 'wins both or it does not ship'. 50/50 probability averaging, each model fed crops from its OWN .onnx.meta.json geometry (every board cropped twice), beats BOTH parents on ALL THREE eval sets: user_photos 0.938/0.894 -> 0.956 with hallucinations still 1 (run_f's 12 vanish — run_e's confident 'empty' vetoes them, occupancy returns to run_e's 0.997), chesscog_transfer 0.819/0.856 -> 0.861 (wrongtype 173/121 -> 118), uploads_calibrate 0.592/0.593 -> 0.603, OVERALL 2673/2711 -> 2758 of 3840. Per-square decomposition is the load-bearing part: parents disagree on 658 squares, exactly one is right on 306, the ensemble wins 215 of those (70%) and REGRESSES ON ZERO of the 2539 squares both parents already had right. So it is a strict improvement on the union, not a variance trade. Two-model oracle ceiling is 2845 (0.741); the ensemble captures 35% of the oracle margin over run_f. The residual 995 both-wrong squares are overwhelmingly the dim uploads_calibrate boards that read ~18/64 for every model — no combination of these two geometries touches them. Cost if shipped: two crop passes + two model runs per frame (~2x classifier cost), and the deployed estimator's one-BR_MODEL-one-sidecar seam has to grow to two.

Ensembling two crop classifiers: the weighting knob is FLAT and the pre-registered 50/50 was also the empirical winner, so do not tune it post-hoc. Measured on run_e+run_f over 3840 squares: prob 50/50 = 2758 correct, prob 30/70 (f-heavy) 2753, logit 50/50 2740, prob 70/30 (e-heavy) 2716 — only the e-heavy option is clearly bad (it throws away the chesscog gain, 0.861 -> 0.843, buying no user_photos accuracy). Probability- vs logit-averaging barely differed (97.4% identical predictions) ONLY because these two models sit on nearly the same confidence scale: mean max-softmax 0.8925 vs 0.8793, mean logit spread 3.45 vs 2.96. That is luck, not a law — arithmetic averaging follows the loudest vote FOR a class while logit (geometric) averaging lets either model VETO one, so a scale mismatch would split them. No temperature artifact is stored for any run (the .onnx.meta.json sidecars carry geometry only; board_reader_inference.calibration fits T at serve time), and the known 'temperature changes 0 argmaxes' result is a SINGLE-model property — it does not carry to averaging, where relative confidence is the whole mechanism. Fit T per model and this table must be re-measured. Gotcha when reading aggregate tables: logit_50_50 and prob_70_30 printed byte-identical SquareStats on uploads_calibrate while actually agreeing on only 94.6% of squares — equal aggregates are not equal predictions, check agreement before concluding two combiners are the same.

How to evaluate a multi-model combiner cheaply and honestly (pattern, see scratch/experiments/ensemble_ef/script.py): (1) REUSE tools/train/evaluate.py's loaders (load_user_photos / load_uploads_calibrate / load_style) and metrics.SquareStats verbatim — a bespoke label loader is how a comparison silently stops being comparable; (2) gate on REPRODUCING each single model's published eval numbers through your harness before believing any combined number (run_e 0.938/0.592/0.819 = 2673, run_f 0.894/0.593/0.856 = 2711) — cheap and it is the only thing standing between you and a preprocessing bug that looks like a result; (3) refuse a missing .onnx.meta.json instead of inheriting evaluate.py's silent bbox fallback, since a model scored on the wrong crops fails quietly; (4) run ONE inference pass, cache raw logits to npz, and derive every combiner and every follow-up analysis from the cache — the whole 60-board 2-model sweep is 4 min on CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' + CPUExecutionProvider, intra_op 6 threads), so no GPU is needed and other work keeps the card; (5) always report the ORACLE (either model right) and the rescued/regressed split alongside the accuracy — 'beats both parents' is weak evidence, 'zero regressions out of 2539 both-right squares' is what tells you the gain is structural. Preprocessing must be byte-identical to evaluate.OnnxPredictor._prep (BGR->RGB via [:, :, ::-1], cv2.INTER_AREA to 224, /255, ImageNet norm outside the graph, NCHW).

The DECOUPLED two-stage decision (variant C: occupancy from run_e/bbox, piece type from run_f/pose with empty masked) is ANSWERED-NEGATIVE and LOSES to plain 50/50 probability averaging on every eval set: user_photos 0.928 vs 0.956, uploads_calibrate 0.576 vs 0.603, chesscog_transfer 0.859 vs 0.861, OVERALL 2688 vs 2758 of 3840 (-70 squares). It fails the pre-registered gate on user_photos (0.928 < 0.93) and is even below run_e alone there (0.938). The premise is what's broken, and the subtask decomposition proves it: 'run_e owns occupancy, run_f owns piece type' is TRUE ONLY on chesscog_transfer (occ 0.9539 vs 0.9508 e-wins; type 0.6843 vs 0.7752 f-wins). On user_photos run_e is better at BOTH (occ 0.9969 vs 0.9625, type 0.8550 vs 0.8321), and on uploads_calibrate the assignment is exactly REVERSED (occ 0.7344 vs 0.7527 f-wins, type 0.4786 vs 0.4250 e-wins). A fixed geometry->subtask routing therefore needs per-SET knowledge you do not have at inference time, while averaging needs none. The mirror control settles it: swapping the roles (occupancy from pose, type from bbox) scores BETTER overall than the hypothesised direction (2698 vs 2688) and posts the best uploads_calibrate number of any combiner (0.609). Occupancy threshold is not the missing lever either — tau in {0.3,0.5,0.7} moves nothing (98.8-99.7% identical predictions to argmax). Consequence: do NOT split occupancy and piece type into separate heads on separate geometries on the strength of the run_e/run_f contrast; hard routing discards the mutual correction that makes averaging work, since under averaging either model can override the other per square.

run_e⊕run_f 50/50 probability ensemble (each model cropping with its OWN sidecar geometry) is deploy-worthy and beats BOTH single models on EVERY eval set: user_photos 0.938→0.956 (halluc still 1, wrongtype 19→13), chesscog_transfer 0.856→0.861 (wrongtype 118), OVERALL 0.696→0.718 — the measured complementary-error prediction held. The decoupled 'routing' variant (occupancy decided by run_e alone, type by run_f alone) is ANSWERED-NEGATIVE: 0.928 user_photos, loses to plain averaging on every set (−70 squares overall) because each model still carries real signal for the task it 'lost' — so combine evidence across crop geometries, don't route decisions to one geometry. Artifacts + preregistration: scratch/experiments/ensemble_ef/. Deploying needs two ONNX sessions + two crop passes (~2× inference) and ensemble support in board_reader_inference.

The run_e⊕run_f ensemble does NOT need 2× inference: a confidence cascade (keep run_e's answer when its max softmax ≥ 0.95, else add run_f and average) recovers the FULL ensemble accuracy on every eval set (user 0.956, chesscog 0.861, OVERALL 0.7182 — identical to always-both) while invoking run_f on only ~30% of squares, i.e. ~1.3× cost. Measured offline from scratch/experiments/ensemble_ef/logits_cache.npz (cascade.py). The gate threshold is NOT sensitive (τ=0.9→0.99 all within noise), so 0.95 is safe without tuning on deployment data. Zero-overhead endgame: distill the averaged-prob teacher into one model.

Central-column patch pooling for DINOv2 does NOT survive at the deployed bank size — the bakeoff's +9 was a small-bank artifact. Reproduced the bakeoff protocol exactly (CLS cross-style 248/320 at an 80-board/5120-exemplar ChessReD bank, same-style LOBO 294/320, both on the nose), then scaled the bank up: central beats CLS 255 vs 248 at 80 boards (+7, but McNemar p=0.27 on 29 discordant squares — never was significant), and the gap VANISHES at the shipped 400-board/25600-exemplar bank: 254 vs 255 (p=1.00). CLS simply catches up when given 5x the exemplars; central does not improve at all (255->254). Same-style LOBO is a dead tie (294 vs 294, 7 discordant each way). Verdict: do not swap the deployed ONNX. The one REAL and significant effect is occupancy: central makes 4 occupancy errors vs CLS's 12 cross-style at 400 boards (net +8, p=0.039), almost entirely by not dropping pieces (missed p->empty 10 -> 1; CLS loses R/N/K to empty, central loses nothing but one pawn). So central pooling is a candidate for an occupancy-specialised head, not a replacement embedding — and the general lesson is that any frozen-backbone A/B measured at one bank size must be re-measured at the size that ships before it is called a win.

models/exemplars_chessred.npz is bit-for-bit sample_boards(per_game=20) over the 20 chessred2k games in that exact order, unaugmented — so board b owns rows [64b, 64b+64) and any board subset can be sliced straight out of the npz instead of re-embedding. Verify before relying on it by rebuilding the label list (ChessReD(...).labels for the sampled ids) and comparing to the npz's labels array; it matches exactly. This is what makes bank-size sweeps cheap, and it guarantees two backbones under comparison see the same boards. Embedding cost is the whole budget of these experiments: DINOv2-S/224 on CPU runs ~5-13 img/s depending on contention, so a 400-board bank is 25600 crops = 30-70 min. Also note tools/build_exemplar_bank_chessred.py crops ALL boards before embedding any (~3.9 GB resident at 400 boards); embed board-by-board instead when other agents are on the box.

Central-column pooling swap is ANSWERED-NEGATIVE (STATUS Next#5 closed 2026-08-11): the bakeoff's +9 over CLS was measured against the weak 80-board bank config and does not survive the shipped 400-board bank — at 400 boards CLS 255/320 vs central 254/320 (tie), same-style LOBO 294 vs 294 (tie), so the ONNX swap + bank rebuilds buy zero accuracy. Two things DO survive: (1) bank SIZE was the bigger lever all along (CLS 80→400 boards = 248→255 cross-style, same +7 the pooling bought); (2) central pooling is genuinely better at cross-style OCCUPANCY (piece→empty misses 10→1 at 400 boards) at the cost of type — so if a zero-setup occupancy-only head ever ships, embed it with central pooling. Bank artifact kept at models/exemplars_chessred_central.npz; scoring in scratch/experiments/central_pooling/. Also: the shipped exemplars_chessred.npz reproduces sample_boards(per_game=20) bit-for-bit, so board subsets slice out by row range without re-embedding.

Calibration-time fine-tune (chesscog candidate #2) is ANSWERED, and the active ingredient is NOT what the paper implies: it is CAPTURE-CONDITION DIVERSITY in the calibration set, not the number of photos or the fine-tuning itself. Controlled at 3 frames of the SAME physical board (user_photos = 5 mid-game photos held out, never trained on, 3 seeds each): 3 frames from ONE session scores 0.932 [0.928-0.938] vs run_e's 0.938 baseline (no gain, and it DAMAGES other boards: other_boards 0.928->0.829, chesscog_transfer 0.819->0.801); 3 frames from THREE sessions scores 0.969 [0.966-0.972] with wrongtype 19->7 AND chesscog_transfer 0.819->0.856. Going to 5 frames/3 sessions adds nothing (0.967). The pre-registered chesscog-parity arm (2 frames, one session, LP-FT 100@1e-3 + 150@1e-4, 5 seeds) FAILED all three gates: 0.935 [0.931-0.947] acc, halluc 1.4 vs 1, wrongtype 19.4 vs 19. Mechanism, from per-class recall: the single-session fine-tune memorises the session (train frames 0.930->1.000, a same-lighting held-out frame 59->64/64) and trades error classes at net zero -- it fixes p->b (recall 0.719->0.925) while breaking B (1.0->0.5), R (1.0->0.78), K, b. The multi-session fine-tune instead makes a REAL, TRANSFERABLE fix to dark pieces: black-pawn recall 0.719->0.990 on user_photos and 0.349->0.728 on chesscog_transfer (a DIFFERENT physical board, 146 crops), q->b eliminated (q recall 0.400->1.000, the decapitation confusion), paying with white N (0.900->0.642) and R (0.700->0.550) on chesscog. So this is not board calibration at all, it is REAL-PHOTO DOMAIN ADAPTATION of a mostly-synthetic-trained model, and three photos are enough if they span lighting. Reconciliation with the paper: chesscog's 9.33->0.11 was measured WITHIN ONE SESSION -- their 27 test images are 'obtained by playing a game of chess and taking a photo after each move', one sitting -- so their result is the within-session case we reproduce (59->64) and never the cross-condition one. Their piece-classifier schedule is also 100@1e-3 then 50@1e-4, not 150.

WiSE-FT (weight-space interpolation back toward the base model, Wortsman et al. arXiv:2109.01903) is a free and apparently strict win on top of a fine-tune here, and costs nothing to try: one lerp of the state_dict, no retraining, no extra inference cost (unlike a probability ensemble, which needs two model runs). On the C2 multi-session calibration fine-tune, alpha=0.75 (weight on the fine-tuned model) beat BOTH parents on EVERY eval set simultaneously: user_photos 0.9375 base / 0.9656 tuned -> 0.9719, other_boards 0.9281 / 0.9281 -> 0.9406, chesscog_transfer 0.8187 / 0.8555 -> 0.8641. A 50/50 probability ensemble of the same two models was WORSE than the alpha-0.75 lerp on all three (0.9688 / 0.9344 / 0.8570) while costing 2x inference -- so reach for the weight lerp before the ensemble when the two models share an initialisation (they do here: one is a fine-tune of the other, so the loss basin is shared and averaging weights is meaningful; this does NOT hold for independently-trained models like run_e vs run_f, where only output-space averaging is defined). Caveat: single seed, and alpha was picked from a 3-point sweep scored on the same sets, so the number is selection-inflated -- re-measure before shipping. Interpolate only the floating-point tensors; num_batches_tracked is integer and must be copied, not lerped.

20 of the 35 data/uploads *-calibrate boards have a ROTATED CORNER ORDER: their sidecar 'corners' are not in a8,h8,h1,a1 order, so the START_PLACEMENT labels the eval harness derives do not match the pixels. The tell is unmistakable once you look: run_e scores 17-26/64 on exactly those 20 and 56-64/64 on the other 15, and their rectified warps show the pieces standing in COLUMNS instead of ranks. Consequence: the project's uploads_calibrate figure (run_e 0.592) is mostly measuring a label bug, not dim-light difficulty, so every A/B that has used uploads_calibrate as a 'hard dim boards' signal has been reading a mixture of two unrelated things -- prefer the 15 sound boards, or repair first. This is the SAME failure chesscog_transfer had before repair_orientation.py (0.500 -> 0.819) and the same fix applies: checkerboard parity of empty cells resolves the 90-degree ambiguity (a8 must be light), light-vs-dark piece wood the 180. Second gotcha in the same directory: data/uploads holds at least FIVE physical boards, not one, and timestamps do NOT delimit capture sessions -- the 9 sound red_white frames span 8 minutes and 3 apparent 'sessions' but share a BYTE-IDENTICAL corner sidecar (0.0 px shift, 5-9 grey levels apart), i.e. one unmoved camera, so they are duplicates. Test near-duplication by corner shift + pixel diff, never by clock gap; on the user's own board every frame differs by 142-1134 px of corner position and IS a genuine separate capture.

Calibration-time fine-tune (chesscog recipe, LP-FT on start-position crops): the two-frames-from-one-session form is ANSWERED-NEGATIVE (user_photos 0.935 vs 0.938 baseline, prereg failed on all three conditions) — but the exploratory sweep found the decisive variable is SESSION DIVERSITY, not frame count: 3 frames from 3 different lighting sessions, same recipe, takes the user's board 0.938→0.969 [0.966–0.972 over seeds] with wrongtype 19→7, occupancy held, held-out same-board frames 0.998, and NO forgetting (chesscog_transfer 0.819→0.856, it gains). Single-session frames are worthless for tuning no matter how many. Product shape: trigger the fine-tune only when a board's stored calibrate frames span ≥3 sessions. Needs one confirming pre-registered run before productionizing. Artifacts: scratch/experiments/calib_finetune/.

uploads_calibrate is NOT a valid comparison set until repaired: 20 of the 25 non-user-board entries have ROTATED corner order in their sidecar labels (run_e scores 17-26/64 on them — label bug, not model failure), which has been silently flooring EVERY model's uploads_calibrate number at ~0.59 (run_e 0.592, run_f 0.593, ensembles ~0.60 — now explained). Same failure mode as the chesscog_transfer 180-degree repair (90b706f, 14 of 22 rotated); the photometric repair (checkerboard parity of empties + piece-wood colour) should apply. Found while building the calib-finetune split manifest, scratch/experiments/calib_finetune/split_manifest.json documents which boards.

Experiment scripts under scratch/experiments/ that import torch must be run with scratch/torchvenv/bin/python, NOT 'uv run python'. The uv workspace is torch-free by design (CLAUDE.md), so 'uv run' fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch' the moment the script imports it. tools/train/_env.sh encodes this (PY defaults to $ROOT/scratch/torchvenv/bin/python) but scratch experiment runners bypass _env.sh and silently inherit the wrong interpreter.

Calibration fine-tune (LP-FT of run_e on start-position crops from >=3 lighting sessions of one board): the ACCURACY gain replicates across fresh seeds (user_photos 0.938 -> 0.968 on seeds 10-14, matching 0.969 on seeds 0-2), but the two arms fail a per-error-type rule because they spend the error budget differently. 3-frame/3-session cuts wrongtype 19->7 while raising hallucinations 1->3.2; 5-frame/3-session keeps hallucinations at 1.8 but leaves wrongtype at 10.4. So gate this recipe on the error DECOMPOSITION, not on accuracy alone -- accuracy alone would have shipped a model that invents pieces on empty squares. WiSE-FT (interpolating tuned weights back toward base, alpha~0.75) is the pending candidate for buying the occupancy budget back; it looked clean on one exploratory seed and needs its own pre-registered multi-seed run.

Multi-session calibration fine-tune, confirming run (fresh seeds 10-14): NOT CONFIRMED as a drop-in replacement for run_e — the accuracy gain REPLICATES robustly (user_photos 0.938→0.968 [0.963–0.975], q→b decapitation confusion goes to zero, q recall 0.40→1.00, no forgetting on chesscog 0.846-0.863) but the occupancy guard fails by a hair in each arm (3-frame arm: halluc 1→3.2 vs rule ≤2; 5-frame arm: wrongtype 10.4 vs rule ≤10). Pattern to remember: EVERY single-model intervention that improves piece type on this task pays a small occupancy tax (run_f's pose crops, now the fine-tune) — type-vs-occupancy is a coupled trade in single 13-way heads, and the fix each time was AVERAGING with a base model, not replacement. Registered follow-up: tuned⊕run_e 50/50. scratch/experiments/calib_finetune_confirm/.

Cascade serving (BR_MODEL + BR_MODEL_B, board_reader_inference.trained.CascadeEstimator) reproduces the run_e⊕run_f experiment BIT-FOR-BIT through the shipped serving code: user_photos 0.9563, uploads_calibrate 0.6027, chesscog_transfer 0.8609, OVERALL 0.7182 (2758/3840), model B invoked on 29.7% of squares — identical to scratch/experiments/ensemble_ef/report.md. That equality is the real preprocessing/geometry verification, stronger than models/deploy_fixture/ (which pins an OLD model, scratch/runs/val_chesscog, and is not wired into any test). To re-check after touching cropping or preprocessing, score the three eval sets through TrainedEstimator.square_dist directly; do NOT import tools/train/evaluate.py (it pulls torch, and the workspace venv is deliberately torch-free) — inline its three loaders, tools/train/styles.py itself is torch-free and gives chesscog_transfer. Also: 'full ensemble' cannot be expressed as tau>1 (rejected) NOR reliably as tau=1.0 — a saturated float32 softmax max is exactly 1.0 and '< 1.0' is False, so saturated squares never defer; at tau=1.0 real models do defer everywhere only because their maxima fall short of 1.0.

Testing a multi-model estimator needs a fake keyed on CROP CONTENT, not call order. A fake logits_fn scripted by call position cannot catch the cascade asking model B about the wrong squares (it maps 'unsure' local indices back onto board indices), and it cannot prove each member cropped with its OWN geometry. The pattern that catches both (packages/inference/tests/test_cascade.py::ScriptedModel): pre-cut the 64 crops for that member's geometry, run them through trained.preprocess(), and key the scripted logits on each row's .tobytes() — bit-exact, since the estimator calls the same preprocess. Two gotchas: (1) key on the PREPROCESSED tensor, not the uint8 crop — un-normalizing float32 back to uint8 is not exact; (2) do NOT use render_board() as the photo — its identical empty squares collapse to 46 distinct crops out of 64. Use seeded uint8 noise.

The 'trained component' of the estimator stack is now a union, not a class: TrainedReader = TrainedEstimator | CascadeEstimator (board_reader_inference.trained). Anything reaching for the zero-shot member must accept both — EstimatorSession.base_trained() returns TrainedReader|None, and it is what /calibrate's orientation probe, bootstrap_bank and refresh_bank all go through, so narrowing it back to TrainedEstimator silently disables bank bootstrapping under a cascade with no test failure outside those paths. The seam that makes two geometries possible is TrainedEstimator.square_dist(image, corners, squares=None) -> (N,13): it crops with the member's OWN geometry and takes a square subset, so a second model pays only for the squares it is asked about. Geometry provenance is now explicit too: TrainedEstimator.geometry_source is 'sidecar'|'explicit'|'fallback', and CascadeEstimator refuses any member on 'fallback' — the lone-model warn-and-assume fallback is fine for one legacy model but poisons an ensemble invisibly.

uploads_calibrate is REPAIRED (tools/repair_upload_orientation.py, 2026-08-11): 14 of 19 rotated sidecars fixed, uploads_calibrate run_e 0.5915->0.7397, run_f 0.5933->0.7156, run_e+run_f 50/50 and the tau=0.95 cascade both 0.6027->0.7415 (they are identical to the square on this set; run_e's max-softmax almost never clears 0.95 here, so the cascade IS the average). Three method lessons that generalise beyond this set. (1) Score piece SIDE (empty/white/black), not exact type, when using a model to resolve a rotation: on the full 13 classes the true rotation led the runner-up by only 6-10/64 on unfamiliar sets (too thin to act on); on side it led by 22-32. (2) A start position's occupancy is 180-symmetric, so the four rotation scores have a fingerprint - true rotation high, its 180 sibling ~32/64 (all empties right, no pieces), the two quarter-turns ~22 (occupancy destroyed). Seeing that profile is itself confirmation the corner order, not the model, was the problem. (3) The diagnostic for a rotated label set is the OCCUPANCY split, not accuracy: run_e's hallucinations went 254->30 and occupancy 0.734->0.934 with no model change.

The photometric orientation repair (repair_orientation.py / repair_upload_orientation.py) has ONE structural blind spot: it assumes the physical board obeys the a8-light convention. The 5 dim_dark frames in data/uploads are set up a quarter-turn off (a8 is DARK), and there the parity test does not merely fail - it returns a CONFIDENT WRONG answer (+24.8 on the perpendicular axis), because on the wrong axis the label's 'empty' cells land on real pieces and it measures piece contamination instead of squares. Only the piece-wood gate (margin +8.1 < the +10 floor) stopped a bad write. How to check a board for this before trusting parity: measure parity over the MIDDLE FOUR RANKS at k=0 and k=2 only - those cells are genuinely empty in a start position and 180 preserves parity, so the two must agree to within a grey level; if the value is negative, a8 is dark and the photometric channel is inapplicable, use the model side-score plus a rendered warp instead. Corollary gotcha: in a dim photo the 'white' pieces sitting in shadow can read DARKER than the light board squares, which inverts the piece-wood test too.

uploads_calibrate mixes THREE populations and its headline number is their weighted average, not a model property - do not A/B models on the whole set. Post-repair run_e 0.7397 decomposes into: 17 original-photo boards with real corner clicks 0.919 (the number comparable to user_photos), 13 boards that are not photos at all 0.633, and the 5 still-rotated dim_dark frames 0.406. The 13 are already-rectified 384x384 top-down crops uploaded whole, whose sidecar records corners=0,0,384,0,384,384,0,384 (the image bounds), so the harness cuts tall photo-geometry boxes out of a WARP. A headroom sweep shows geometry is only part of it: 0.528 (hr 0.0) / 0.633 (1.6, deployed) / 0.675 (2.2) / 0.680 (2.8, peak) / 0.656 (3.4) / 0.639 (4.0) - a warp's pieces smear further in units of square width than a photo's so 1.6 under-crops them, but even at the peak they sit 24 points below the photo boards; the crop-domain gap is the bulk. Spot these entries by image shape 384x384 or by corners equal to the image bounds.

Composition beats replacement for the calibration fine-tune, and for the same reason it did for run_e+run_f: a 50/50 probability average of the fine-tuned model with base run_e keeps the piece-type win (wrongtype 19 -> ~9) while pinning empty->piece hallucinations back to the base model's 1 -- on all 10 runs across 2 arms x 5 seeds, never once above 1. Both arms FAIL the five-condition rule as drop-in replacements and both PASS composed. Rule of thumb for this project: when a fine-tune trades occupancy for type, average it with the base rather than tuning the recipe -- the base model's occupancy confidence outvotes the tuned model's over-eagerness on empty squares.

scratch/experiments runners must persist the trained checkpoints (torch.save of state_dict per seed) even when the immediate question only needs scores. calib_finetune_confirm/confirm.py freed each model after scoring, so the registered follow-up (compose tuned with run_e) had to retrain all 10 seeds -- ~20 min of GPU -- and 2 of 10 did not reproduce exactly (cuDNN nondeterminism: acc +/-0.003, wrongtype +/-2), which weakens any post-hoc comparison against the original table. A per-seed state_dict is ~45 MB for resnet18; cheap insurance against exactly this.

Calibration fine-tune, final form (2026-08-11, all pre-registered): tuned⊕run_e 50/50 composition PASSES every condition on fresh seeds — user_photos 0.938→0.969, wrongtype 19→9, hallucinations exactly 1 on all ten composed runs (identical to run_e: the composition never invents a piece the base would not), chesscog_transfer 0.819→0.853-0.858 (no forgetting). Mechanism, same as run_e⊕run_f: base occupancy confidence outvotes the tuned model's over-eagerness on empties; tuned type confidence carries occupied squares. Recommended production recipe: 3 start-position frames from 3 DIFFERENT lighting sessions, LP-FT (head 100@1e-3 then all 150@1e-4, train_transform aug), served as 50/50 average with the base model — 3 frames ties 5 frames (0.9688 vs 0.9694, 0.2 squares) and costs the user less. Deployment trigger: only when a board's stored calibrate frames span ≥3 sessions. Epistemic caveat on record: seed robustness tested twice, new-data generalization ZERO times (same 5 user_photos throughout) — own footage is the real test. scratch/experiments/calib_finetune_confirm/report.md.

BR_MODEL_TUNED (AveragedEstimator) reproduces the calib_finetune experiment EXACTLY through the shipped serving code: on the 5 user_photos boards, run_e base = 0.9375 (300/320, halluc 1, wrongtype 19) — the experiment's sanity gate to the digit — and tuned⊕base = 0.9688 (310/320, halluc 1, missed 0, wrongtype 9), matching the report's C2' ⊕ run_e row exactly. The tuned model ALONE scores 0.9656 with halluc 4: the hallucination tax is real and the base's vote is what removes it, so the server's refusal to run BR_MODEL_TUNED without BR_MODEL is load-bearing, not ceremony. To re-verify after touching cropping/preprocessing, score through TrainedEstimator/AveragedEstimator.square_dist directly and inline the ground_truth.json loader — do NOT import tools/train/evaluate.py (it pulls torch, the workspace venv is torch-free). Gotcha in that loader: data/eval/ground_truth.json has 10 records but 5 of them (up_2026*) have neither their data/uploads source nor a *_rect.png sibling any more, so 'user_photos' means the 5 img_05xx boards / 320 squares — a scorer that does not skip missing sources dies on imread returning None.

tools/train/calibrate_finetune.py keeps torch OUT of module scope on purpose (every torch/cv2/_bootstrap import lives inside the function that needs it), so its frame-loading + session-clustering layer imports in the torch-free workspace venv. That is what lets the >=3-capture-session product gate be unit-tested by 'make test': pyproject testpaths names the single FILE tools/train/tests/test_calibrate_finetune.py rather than the directory, so torch-importing test_dataset.py stays out. Two traps if you extend it: (1) do NOT import _bootstrap at module scope — it installs a STUB board_reader_inference package into sys.modules, which would poison every later test in the same xdist worker; (2) an argparse tool that recommends 'BR_MODEL=<sibling model.onnx>' must verify the sibling really is that checkpoint's export (random batch through torch vs onnxruntime, atol 1e-3) — a stale sibling from an earlier export would silently pair the fine-tune with a base it was never fine-tuned from, and nothing downstream can detect it. Runtime: 3 frames x 64 crops, 250 LP-FT iters = ~56 s on the GTX 1650.

board-reader has TWO entry points that start a real inference node — 'docker compose up' (compose.yaml) and 'make dev' (the Makefile) — and each picks its recognition composition out of the same BR_* environment independently. They drifted silently: the confidence-gated cascade landed in compose.yaml alone (2b64ada) and 'make dev' kept serving BR_MODEL by itself for two days, so every live phone test rehearsed a measurably weaker reader than the demo it was rehearsing for, and nothing failed — no test covered it and aspects.yaml's 'deploy' aspect listed only compose.yaml/docker/**, so /drift could not see the Makefile half either. Two fixes that generalise: (1) when an aspect is described as 'how the system is actually run', its files list must contain EVERY entry point, not just the containerised one; (2) parity between a Makefile and a config file is testable without starting anything — 'make -n dev' prints the fully-resolved recipe including conditional env, so a test can read the env make WOULD forward and compare it to the compose service, which also exercises the makefile conditionals rather than pattern-matching variable definitions. Pass overrides on the command line (make -n dev BR_MODEL=<a file that exists>) so the assertion tests declared intent and stays green on a fresh clone with no models/ dir.

On /camera, the page-level base rule `.camera :global(button)` (in +page.svelte: accent fill, 9px radius, 15px, min-height 48) has specificity (0,2,1) after Svelte scoping. A component rule written as a single class — `.pill`, `.text-btn` — is only (0,2,0) and LOSES to it, so the component's own look silently never applies: the overlay cluster rendered as solid blue rectangles and the sheet's text links as blue buttons with an underline. Nothing warns; svelte-check and every geometry-based e2e assertion still pass. Write component button rules with two classes (`.cluster .pill`, `.row .text-btn`) so they clear (0,2,1). A bare `.hint-bar button` (0,2,1) does win, but only on source order — component styles land after page styles — so don't rely on that. camera.spec.ts now pins the pills' translucency and radius for this reason.

Playwright can drive real safe-area insets: `(await page.context().newCDPSession(page)).send('Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride', { insets: { top, right, bottom, left } })` makes env(safe-area-inset-*) resolve to those px in headless Chromium (verified on playwright 1.62.1; the method is in the bundled protocol.d.ts, so it type-checks without casts). That turns notch/home-indicator handling from an unfalsifiable stylesheet reading into a measurement — camera.spec.ts uses it to assert the button cluster and chips move inward while the picture deliberately does not. Assert the DIFFERENCE the inset makes where the flat-screen value would already pass (the sheet's padding-bottom is 24px before any inset, so `>= 21` proves nothing).

To e2e-test anything depending on WHAT the camera sees, replace getUserMedia with a canvas captureStream you draw: Object.defineProperty(navigator.mediaDevices, "getUserMedia", { configurable: true, value: () => Promise.resolve(canvas.captureStream(30)) }) inside page.addInitScript. Two things make PlaneTracker actually hold its lock on a drawn scene: (a) add non-periodic marks — a bare checkerboard is aperture-ambiguous, so a translation of half a square reads as one of one and a half; (b) translate ~4 px per rAF rather than jumping, since a 40 px single-frame jump is outside pyramidal LK basin. Also stub /api/detect with a quad matching the drawn board: the detection lands, sets origin=detected, and automatic detection then stands down — otherwise a detect can own the page activity union when the test taps a control. Measured: the tracker follows a 40 px slide to within ~8 px and stays locked even at 30% contrast. To vary contrast without moving the mean the sharpness score divides by, draw on a mid-grey background that is exactly the mean of the two square colours. Complements the older fake-camera note.

A stopped board-reader inference server can keep its GPU. uvicorn's shutdown can wedge behind an in-flight ONNX call: the process stops listening (so the port frees and nothing looks wrong) but stays resident holding its CUDA context and ~340MB of VRAM, and it ignores SIGTERM — only SIGKILL reaps it. Observed 2026-08-13 after 'make stop' printed 'stopped' unconditionally; the leaked server sat for 2h and the next 'make dev' inherited a card too full for the two-model cascade. Two consequences worth remembering. (1) A released port is NOT evidence a server exited — check 'nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv', not 'ss -ltn'. (2) OpenCV's OpenCL backend is what converts a tight GPU into a CRASH rather than a degradation: a failed warpAffine allocation throws cv::Exception through C++ terminate, aborting the process with status 134, uncatchable from Python. onnxruntime's own OOM surfaces as a catchable RuntimeException by comparison. 'make dev' now sets OPENCV_OPENCL_RUNTIME=disabled (the strong form — the runtime never loads, so it claims no VRAM; OPENCV_OPENCL_DEVICE=disabled only sets useOpenCL False and still loads it). Deliberately not mirrored in compose.yaml, which declares no GPU device and runs the same cascade on CPU: env parity between entry points does not imply the same hardware envelope.

On /camera, a manual "detect board" is a silent NO-OP while an automatic detection is in flight — the page admits one owner of the camera and quad at a time, and an automatic miss deliberately shows no banner. So an e2e that clicks detect to provoke a banner can click into a dead window and hang on the wait. Wrap the whole click-and-wait in expect(async () => {...}).toPass(): retrying the block is the only thing that covers it, since the button is momentarily enabled between attempts. Give the inner wait a generous timeout (~8s, not 3s) — a retry re-encodes and re-posts a 1600px JPEG, and with 6 playwright workers each driving a 20fps capture loop plus tracker, contention alone pushed one such test from 1.7s standalone to 12s in-suite.

/camera layout (packages/viewer/ui/src/lib/components/camera/): a full-bleed picture with floating controls needs the text chrome to DODGE the controls, and the only way to express that in CSS is a hand-computed reservation (--cluster-w: calc(124px + 8px + max(8px, env(safe-area-inset-right))), --cluster-h: calc(8px+48px+8px+48px+inset)) that several rules must independently agree with. Every one of those numbers is a guess about a layout it cannot see — a pill width, a font metric, a phone's text-size setting, an inset — and when one is wrong the right-hand controls run off the screen. It shipped that way and the full Playwright suite (which measures real boundingBoxes, in both orientations, with CDP safe-area overrides) still passed, because Chromium's defaults happened to satisfy every guess. Replace it with a layout that CANNOT hold a wrong number: one fixed overflow:hidden stage, safe-area insets taken ONCE there as padding (so no component below reads env() at all), and a single flex line 'frame | rail' whose flex-direction is the entire landscape/portrait difference. The rail is flex:0 0 auto with white-space:nowrap pills, so its width IS its widest label; the frame is flex:1 1 auto with min-width/min-height:0; the status strip lives inside the frame so 'left:0;right:0' already stops at the buttons. It costs no picture: on an 844x390 landscape stage with a 16:9 camera the picture measures 693x390 either way, because the letterbox already exceeded the rail (re-confirms the older 'inset the picture from the chrome' learning that this reversal overrode). Per-device breakpoints go too — 'min-height: clamp(44px, 12vh, 48px)' + 'gap: clamp(4px, 1.6vh, 10px)' fits six pills continuously from 320px to 390px of landscape height where three @media (max-height) steps used to. Test it as DISJOINT BOXES (rail.x >= frame.x + frame.width) rather than as arithmetic that comes out right.

The inference node's GPU is usually also the DISPLAY pipeline, and the display is the side that cannot degrade. With the common Optimus layout (optimus-manager 'integrated' + AllowNVIDIAGPUScreens; xrandr --listproviders shows NVIDIA-G0 as cap 0x2 Sink Output ONLY) an external monitor is rendered by the iGPU and copied into a reverse-PRIME surface in NVIDIA VRAM for scanout. X reallocates that surface on DPMS wake / mode set / monitor re-probe, and if the card is full at that instant there is no fallback: 'Failed to allocate reverse prime surface: out of memory' and 'Failed to allocate memory for composition pipeline' in /var/log/Xorg.0.log, and if the failed DPMS-on leaves the HDMI link down the following EDID read returns nothing and the mode pool is EMPTIED ('Unable to add nvidia-auto-select mode to ModePool') so the monitor vanishes from xrandr. Happened twice on 2026-08-13; the second was 60s after a /calibrate (data/uploads/*-calibrate.jpg and models/exemplars_session.npz mtimes pin it). Recover with 'xrandr --output HDMI-1-0 --mode 1920x1080' then back to 3840x2160 — no reboot. Note the diagnostic trap: ~/.local/share/xorg/Xorg.0.log can be years stale, the live log is /var/log/Xorg.0.log, and kernel timestamps from early boot can be off by the UTC offset until NTP corrects them. Fix shipped: cuda_providers() now returns ('CUDAExecutionProvider', options) with gpu_mem_limit (BR_GPU_MEM_LIMIT_MB, default 1024 MiB), arena_extend_strategy=kSameAsRequested and cudnn_conv_algo_search=HEURISTIC, plus 'make dev-cpu'. MEASURED sizing on the 4GB GTX 1650, all three models are 224px: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 at batch 64 FAILS at a 768 MiB cap and passes at 896 (one batch-64 attention matrix is 101 MB); the two ResNet18s need <768; the real three-session process peaks at ~1.6 GiB. Lowering the embedder batch 64->32 saves only ~50 MiB of the process total (1618->1566) because the retained classifier arenas dominate — not worth the throughput. The cap is PER SESSION (ORT only shares an arena via the env-allocator API, which we do not use), so the default is a band: >=896 to run, <=1365 so 3x still leaves a 4 GiB card ~1 GiB.

CLI-set env vars never reach an import-time app: board_reader_inference/__init__.py imports server, so a module-level 'app = create_app()' ran at package import — BEFORE cmd_serve set BR_RECORD_DIR/BR_CENTROIDS — and uvicorn.run('server:app') then reused that stale app. Result: every 'make dev'/bare-serve run since WP-H2 recorded NOTHING, while docker compose (env set before the process) recorded fine — an asymmetry that masked the bug. The fix and the rule: no module-level app in a package whose __init__ imports the module; serve with uvicorn.run('module:create_app', factory=True) after setting env (the viewer already did this for a different reason). Symptom to recognise: a flag that 'does nothing' only when passed via the CLI.

A refused /ingest frame is invisible server-side unless counted: refusal happens in the WS handler before FrameIngest.submit and before recording, and its reason went only to the phone's banner — so 'every frame refused' and 'never sent' were indistinguishable from the node. frames_refused now rides healthz.ingest and each refusal logs at WARNING. When a phone trial leaves an empty recordings/ dir, check three hypotheses in order: stream never connected (client-logs/), all frames refused (healthz refused counter), recording itself broken (the import-time-app bug).

Live-path reads are materially worse than calibration-frame reads on the same scene: /camera streams a cropBox'd 960px q75 JPEG while /calibrate posts the full-res frame — replaying the 20260813-182222 calibration frame through the live encoding turned a 64/64 read (0.88 conf) into rnbkkbnr (two black kings, d8 q->k, a-file pawns lost at the crop edge, 0.79 conf). The bank never contains live-domain exemplars, so 'calibrated 13/13' does not predict stream quality. The prior decoder repairs the impossible reads (kings constraint, ~0.7 nats) but repairs to A possible board, not necessarily the right square — treat red-ringed flips as uncertainty markers. To reproduce a live read offline: crop to corner bbox, scale long side to 960, imencode q75, POST /estimate with rebased corners.

Phone-camera recovery on /camera has three layers that MUST cooperate: (1) MediaStreamTrack ended/mute/unmute listeners (guard 'stream !== next' — a replaced lens's tracks end too), (2) visibilitychange/pageshow, (3) a video.currentTime watchdog (state.ts noteFrameClock, play->reopen with backoff). Two review-caught traps: iOS suspends setInterval while backgrounded, so the watchdog's 'hidden resets grace' branch may never run — the visible handler must reset the clock itself (freshFrameClock) or the first tick after return reads a 30s stall and reopens before play() gets a chance; and getUserMedia can outlive the reopen backoff, so ALL openCamera calls are serialized through one promise queue (and recoverCamera has an in-flight guard) — two interleaved opens each stopTracks() what the other was starting, and the loser's stream keeps the camera claimed with nothing pointing at it.

Scoring a trial recording needs NO model and no GPU: events.ndjson already carries all three published boards (raw placement, prior.placement, settled.placement), so board_reader_inference.trial scores 85 events in ~0.1s. The load-bearing measurement design: score the three streams APART, never summed. On recordings/20260813-193308 (81 scored events, 5 truth segments) raw and prior land on effectively the SAME per-square total — 5010/5184 vs 5005/5184 — while their perfect-board rates differ by infinity: 0/81 vs 20/81. The prior decoder fixes the persistent d8 q->k (78 raw confusions) but pays for it with a k->q/q->k flip-flop (52/53 each way), so a per-square headline says 'the repair is neutral' about a change that turns an unusable stream into a quarter-usable one. Two gotchas found building it: (1) the settled block did not exist when older recordings were made, so it must be DERIVED by replaying BoardStabilizer over the event sequence — and it must be fed EVERY event including the guard-excluded ones, because the live gateway saw those too and a debounce that skips them settles differently; (2) truth for a trial is a step function over frame seq, not a set of photos, and the boundary needs a guard window (guard_seqs, ~12 seqs = 1.5s at 7.5fps) because the operator's boundary is an instant while the hand-over-the-board occlusion is a window — without it every move costs several fabricated 'errors'.

Exporting crops that tools/train can actually consume: the chain is styles.py (discovers data/external/**/labels_normalized.json) -> cropcache.py (shards) -> dataset.py (torch). Two schemas are auto-detected from the FIRST record: board-level needs 'corners_a8_h8_h1_a1'+'placement', crop-level needs 'piece'+'chess_set'. For already-cut square crops emit crop-level {image, piece, chess_set}; 'piece' takes a bare FEN letter or the literal 'empty', and empty-square records are pooled and copied into EVERY style (empties are style-agnostic), so their chess_set is ignored. The style name tools/train ends up using is '<manifest dir name>_<chess_set>', not anything in the file. THE GEOMETRY TRAP: cropcache.py declares HEADROOM = 0.15 with the comment 'Deployed photo-crop geometry (must match the gateway)' and that is STALE — the deployed run_e sidecar (models/run_e/model.onnx.meta.json) is headroom 1.6 / side_pad 0.15, which is squares.DEFAULT_GEOMETRY. Cutting export crops at 0.15 decapitates every piece and the mismatch is invisible until the model 'gets worse'. Always write the geometry dict beside the manifest (board_reader_inference.trial writes export.json) — a pre-cut crop whose geometry is unknown is not reusable data. Filename tip: name crops '<seq>_<square>_<class>.jpg'; (seq, square) is already unique so the P-vs-p class letter never collides on a case-insensitive filesystem.

Choosing WHICH surplus king to demote must compare p(king) evidence per square, not the k→runner-up margin: the margin subtracts a noisy tail log-prob and picked the wrong square 55% on the 08-13 trial replay (628 two-king frames), vs 27% for lowest-p(k). Temporal EMA of square_dist does NOT fix it (misread is systematic, ~43% at any alpha) — smoothing distributions is not a lever against a biased model.

Debounce windows over the position stream must be wall-clock, not read-count: estimator read rate varies >10x with load (0.9/s loaded vs 7.5/s replayed on the same stream), and a K tuned at one rate is wrong at the other (K=3 knee at 0.9/s becomes K~12 at 7.5/s). BoardStabilizer uses seconds + min-reads for this reason.

Recordings replay offline without the server: build the deployed stack with server._default_estimator(None) (env BR_MODEL/BR_SESSION_BANK/BR_MODEL_B as in Makefile), then per frames.ndjson row decode_jpeg + Frame(corners=np.asarray(r['corners'],f32).reshape(4,2)) + route_for(est, frame).read(). events.ndjson strips square_dist BY DESIGN — replay is how you get it back (~1.3s/frame, 748 frames ≈ 16 min). Corners in frames.ndjson are a flat 8-list, reshape before rectify.

A leaning piece near a square boundary reads as THREE errors at once (08-13 trial, knight on c6 leaning into b6): correct square keeps its class, the lean-into square hallucinates a piece-type from the visible fragment (b6=rook from the knight head), and the occluded square behind blends classes (b7 pawn read as bishop). piece_count repair catches the hallucination only when the side already has 16 pieces. Crop attribution needs piece-base weighting, not bounding-prism membership.

A trial recording keeps a top-2-per-square evidence digest, not the full square_dist: server._record_published pops square_dist (~25 kB/line at burst rate) and writes protocol.square_evidence() instead (~1.8 kB). It is the difference between 'd8 read k' and 'd8 read k at 0.51 over q at 0.49' — the margin is what says whether a misread is fixable (truth ranked second by a hair = the crop carries the answer) or hopeless (truth outside the top 2 = the evidence is not there). Digest is of the ESTIMATOR's distribution; the prior repair never rewrites square_dist, so the same evidence underlies all three streams. Recordings made before 2026-08-27 carry none and _parse_evidence returns None rather than fabricating one.

Two board-reader headline accuracies have now died the same death: quoted from a run that left no artifact, unreproducible later (638/640 curated boards, and the 08-13 trial's '66.6% perfect / 98.96% per-square' which re-scores at 25.8% / 97.7%). The 08-13 cause was found: truth.json is hand-authored, git-ignored and EDITABLE after the fact — it went from 5 segments/guard 12 (81 scored events) to 6 segments/guard 25 (66 scored), which moves every rate. So a trial number is only as stable as the truth file behind it. trial.run() now always writes <recording>/report.json (--json only relocates it), which pins truth, streams and counts together in one artifact. When quoting any trial figure, cite the report.json, not a chat message or a STATUS line.

Client-side trial telemetry needs a heartbeat, not just events: the 08-13 phone trial produced 14 client-log lines for 748 frames, all lifecycle/anomaly notes, so a quiet stretch was ambiguous between 'sending happily' and 'sending nothing'. lib/edge/heartbeat.ts samples IngestClient's counters (sent/dropped/acked/connected/behind) every 10s while streaming and notes rates + unacked backlog. Sampling beats counting here: nothing in the capture path has to report to it, and it stays as best-effort as the log it writes into.
